crawl: Chrome live crawl, same-origin fetch, cache: no-store, sequential per URL, ~06:25-06:40 Vietnam time on 2026-10-02 (one-day step from 1 Oct)
method: TTFB measured with performance.now() around a sequential fetch of each URL with a 15 s abort. Words counted on a body clone with script/style/noscript/template removed. Schema blocks counted as application/ld+json elements, @type walked through @graph. Internal links are unique same-origin paths per page.
score_rationale: Health HOLDS at 95 (raw 95.15 -> 94.90), but for the FIRST TIME IN THIS SERIES the two heaviest sub-scores moved in OPPOSITE directions and all but cancelled. CRAWLABILITY 98 -> 99: the site-wide promoted link the article template dropped on 28 Sep is RESTORED. Exactly 94 of the 95 articles each gained exactly +1 distinct internal link, total distinct internal links moved 2,711 -> 2,805 after sitting at 2,711 for THREE consecutive crawls, and the average per page rose 23.0 -> 23.8. The one article that did not move, /articles/bim-3d-from-design-to-site-in-2026, already linked that target from its body copy, so on that page the template link is a duplicate and distinct-path counting shows no increase. HONESTY LIMIT: the exact link TARGET cannot be isolated from a single day's crawl, because the per-target link graph is not stored per day - 20 site-wide targets are now present on all 95 articles. The SHAPE of the change matches the 28 Sep regression being reversed, but the specific target is INFERRED, not measured, and no restored URL is stated here as fact; that is why crawlability reads 99 rather than 100. PERFORMANCE 98 -> 96: TTFB rose across the board - site mean 331 -> 531 ms, median 268 -> 493 ms, ceiling 654 -> 914 ms, core 350 -> 499 ms, articles 328 -> 541 ms, projects 328 -> 453 ms. It is a uniform shift rather than one bad page, and it stays inside a healthy band: all 118 pages still answered in under a second, nothing landed in the 1-3 s band and nothing exceeded 3 s, for an eighth consecutive crawl. The slowest page is now /articles at 914 ms with the homepage second at 868 ms - the two heaviest pages on the site rather than an article, which is a change from 1 Oct. STRUCTURED DATA HOLDS 92, ON-PAGE HOLDS 92 and CONTENT HOLDS 93: all three are BYTE-IDENTICAL to 1 Oct - 116 of 118 pages with schema, 394 JSON-LD blocks, FAQPage frozen at 82 of 95 articles (86.3 pct) for a SIXTH consecutive scan with the same 13 articles missing one; 118/118 for exactly one h1, title, meta description, canonical and self-canonical, zero heading-level skips, 1,387 images with 1,269 alt; 241,211 words, not one word changed, and no new article for an eighth day. Raw 94.90 still rounds half-up to 95, so Health HOLDS at 95 with its two biggest components pulling against each other.

pages.note: 117 sitemap HTML pages plus /login. All 118 returned 200. No new page and no removed page against 1 Oct; the page set is identical for a twenty-second crawl and identical to both 30 Sep and 1 Oct.

sitemap.linked_absent_method: Re-measured this run from the inbound-link graph over all 118 crawled pages, counting only same-origin HTML paths.
sitemap.legacy_recheck_note: The ten legacy long-slug article URLs were re-fetched today from the origin at /articles/<slug>: ten of ten returned 200 with a self-referencing canonical, unchanged - a fifteenth clean recheck.

ttfb_ms.note: TTFB ROSE ACROSS THE BOARD and the shift is uniform rather than one bad page: site mean 331 -> 531 ms, median 268 -> 493 ms, ceiling 654 -> 914 ms, core 350 -> 499 ms, articles 328 -> 541 ms, projects 328 -> 453 ms, core excluding the homepage 339 -> 476 ms. The slowest page is now the /articles hub at 914 ms with the homepage second at 868 ms - the two heaviest pages on the site, not an article, which is a change from 1 Oct when an article led. The floor barely moved, 241 -> 235 ms. Even so all 118 pages answered in under a second, 0 landed in the 1-3 s band and 0 exceeded 3 s, an eighth consecutive crawl. Four cache-busted repeats of the homepage returned 518-805 ms, so run-to-run variance remains wide, but every group moving the same way on the same run makes this a real shift in the distribution rather than noise on one URL.

content.note: The corpus is BYTE-IDENTICAL to 1 Oct at 241,211 words - not one word changed, including the /articles hub at 1,067 words. No article was added or removed for an eighth consecutive day; the last new article was 24 Sep. The average article runs 2,435 words, core pages 521 and project pages 178. The 13 pages under 300 words are exactly the same 13 as on 1 Oct.

schema.note: FAQPage coverage HELD at 82 of 95 articles (86.3 pct) for a SIXTH consecutive scan - the same 13 articles are still without one. 116 of 118 pages carry schema and the JSON-LD block total is unchanged at 394. Every structured-data signal is byte-identical to 1 Oct.

heading_skips.note: No heading level is skipped anywhere on the site.

onpage.note: Byte-identical to 1 Oct on every on-page signal: 118/118 for exactly one h1, title, meta description, canonical and self-canonical; zero heading-level skips; 96 pages still render a heading before their h1; meta descriptions run 83-189 characters. The alt-text gap is unchanged at 118 of 1,387 images (1,269 with alt, 91.5 pct) and is confirmed again this crawl to be EXACTLY ONE image per page - a single template image, so one fix closes all 118.

crawlability.note: THE SITE-WIDE PROMOTED LINK IS BACK. Total distinct internal links moved 2,711 -> 2,805 after three consecutive crawls at 2,711, and the average per page rose 23.0 -> 23.8. Exactly 94 of the 95 articles each gained exactly +1 distinct internal link; the only article that did not move, /articles/bim-3d-from-design-to-site-in-2026, already linked that target from its body copy, so there the template link is a duplicate and distinct-path counting records no increase. The TARGET ITSELF IS NOT MEASURED: the per-target link graph is not stored per day, 20 site-wide targets are now present on all 95 articles, and no single restored URL can be isolated from one day of crawling - the shape of the change matches the 28 Sep template regression being reversed, but that is an INFERENCE, not a measurement. THE OVERLAY FIX HELD FOR A FOURTH DAY: a live load of /articles, waited out 15 seconds, returns zero fixed full-viewport elements at z-index >= 9999 and elementFromPoint at the viewport centre resolves to an ordinary content div. The hub still exposes all 95 articles and carries 112 distinct internal link paths. Zero orphans for a twenty-first day and zero hub-only articles. Hub HTML size was not re-measured on this run.

tag_check.note: Homepage DOM tag check: window.google_tag_manager exposes 17 keys including the GTM container GTM-PZ9N8QTR, the Google Ads tag AW-18039433307 and the GA4 tag G-43HE633LGK. dataLayer length 3. window.gtag is undefined, as on every previous check - GTM loads the tags itself. Identical to 1 Oct.

roadmap: P0 - publish a new article. Eight days without one pins Content at 93 and leaves Google no freshness signal; with the internal-link regression now reversed this is the largest remaining lever.
P1 - batch a FAQPage block into the 13 articles still missing one; coverage has been frozen at 82 of 95 (86.3 pct) for SIX crawls and the method is proven on the other 82.
P1 - add alt text to the single template image repeated on every page. One template fix closes all 118 missing-alt images and clears the last measurable on-page defect.

P2 - watch TTFB for a second day before acting. The site mean rose 331 -> 531 ms, the median 268 -> 493 ms and the ceiling 654 -> 914 ms on a single run, uniformly across core, articles and projects, which is the signature of host-side or network-side change rather than a page problem; all 118 pages are still under a second, so confirm the shift repeats before touching anything.

P3 - confirm which link the article template restored. The +1 on 94 of 95 articles is measured, but the target is inferred from the shape of the 28 Sep regression, not from the crawl; a one-off per-target link-graph capture would settle it and would be what takes crawlability from 99 to 100.
process_note: ONE crawl served both this audit and the SEO report in the same run, so TTFB, word counts, schema counts and the internal-link graph agree between the two reports by construction - the +1 internal link on 94 of 95 articles, the 531 ms site mean and the 241,211-word corpus are the same measurements in both, read once.
